Changelog
=========

1.1.0
  - Other people's .asi mods now load without any setup: drop the .asi into plugins\ (or into a folder of its own
    there) and switch it on in the Mods panel, under "Basic mods". Like every mod it starts off. It is loaded as
    it is: the loader does not check it, and it has no settings or reload in the panel. A .dll is not listed;
    rename it to .asi if its maker says it is an ASI mod.
  - Safe start: when a start does not finish (a mod crashed the game), the next start loads no mods and says so,
    so you can pause and switch the mod off. This covers every mod, the ones with a mod.ini too. Ask for one by
    hand with safe_start=1 under [mods] in ds3_mods.ini. The loader keeps a small file for this,
    ds3_mods_start.ini, next to dinput8.dll. It notices a start that fails in about the first 20 seconds, not a
    crash later on.
  - Ultimate ASI Loader installed as well: the loader notices, leaves .asi files without a mod.ini to it, turns
    hot reload off and says so in the Mods panel. Using both together is not supported.
  - The Mods panel shows a mod's settings only while the mod is loaded; a mod that is off (or did not load) keeps
    just its switch, whose help line says how to see its settings.
  - Mods panel: a help text too long for the bottom of the panel now scrolls instead of being cut off, and the
    mouse cursor is drawn over the pause menu's "mods" button, not behind it.
  - Worked around a rare crash right at the start of the game when no mod was switched on (it was in 1.0.0
    too): the loader now waits a moment before it sets up its drawing.
  - Up to 32 mods (was 16).
  - For mod makers: the check for hot reload (does the mod export DS3ModShutdown) now reads the mod's file
    directly, which no longer depends on how Windows maps it.
  - The six add-ons are unchanged from 1.0.0: if you have them, you don't need the add-ons download again.

1.0.0 (first public release)
  - The DS3 Mod Loader: one proxy DLL (dinput8.dll) that runs drop-in mods from plugins\, with an in-game Mods
    panel (pause > "mods", F11, or Back on a pad) with every mod's switch and the settings it lists. The loader is
    only the framework: every feature is a mod.
  - Optional add-ons, all in one download with a READ ME FIRST.txt that says what each does: Raw Input Mouse Fix, Ration Seal Store, Auto Pickup, Resource Counter,
    Mouse Slider Range, Hello Mod. Each is also an example for mod makers: Mouse Slider Range needs no code (a patch
    mod, only a mod.ini); the others are DLL mods in C++. The source download has the source of all six.
  - The Raw Input Mouse Fix add-on is based on the fix by slopkhayzo (MIT), rebuilt with the SDK; credited in
    THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt. Like every add-on it is off until you switch it on in the Mods panel. Its speed
    follows the game's Mouse Sensitivity slider (UseGameSlider on; at slider 50 the multiplier is 0.50).
  - For mod makers: the SDK, in the source download (sdk\ds3mod.h, API 3), with hot reload, drawing with any Windows font and fading
    boxes, patch mods that need no code, a guide in
    sdk\README.md with a "What you need" list, a step-by-step for moving an existing ASI mod into plugins\, the
    known game addresses (sdk\GAME_NOTES.md), and a read-only memory inspector (sdk\tools\ds3_mcp.py).
  - Made for updates: a new version of a mod is unzipped over the old one, and your switch and settings stay. A mod
    says which loader it needs (min_loader= in its mod.ini), and an older loader shows "needs loader" in the Mods
    panel instead of loading it. The rules for mod makers: sdk\README.md, "Releasing and updating your mod".
  - Source code under the MIT licence.

Before 1.0: private test builds, never released.
